label: L=9 copy step 1 (input = first token o/x/l), gated by tokens 2-3
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, on the step just after the first copy output (t = L+1, recall_idx 1, previous input <DEL>, input = the fed-back first original token), and almost only in length-9 sequences (97.5% of mass at L=9, the rest at L=8). It never fires during the original phase or at the delimiter. Within that slot, the first token matters most: o, x and l together hold about 82% of mass (c, n, v add a bit more); the token being output (orig(1): b, j, z, f) and the next one (orig(2): z, k, b) push it further up. The strongest activations combine these (e.g. o then j/z, l then j/z). The slot alone (recall_idx 1, L 9) gives about 97% recall but 2% precision; the full conjunction gives F1 around 0.45 on dev, so this looks like a sparse, roughly additive mix of first-token and second/third-token contributions that a boolean predicate only partly captures. Magnitudes are tiny (max 0.02).
